passage:
The rain had turned the railway platform into a river, and the station was packed. Baljeet stood under a leaking shed, holding his bag over his head. He had a low opinion of the police since a constable had shouted at him over a small fine the year before.
Then he heard a child crying. A girl of about four stood alone by the bench. Constable Shreya crouched in the wet, took off her own raincoat and put it on the child. "What's your name? Where were you sitting?" She spoke into the radio, called the announcement, and stayed until a woman came sprinting up the platform.
Baljeet thought of the constable who had shouted, and of Shreya. He decided he could not use one word for both.

qa.q: How old did the lost girl seem to be?
qa.a: The girl seemed to be about four.

qa.q: Why did Baljeet have a low opinion of the police at the start?
qa.a: Baljeet felt resentful and hurt because a constable had shouted at him over a small fine the year before.

qa.q: What did Baljeet decide after watching Shreya, and why is it fair?
qa.a: He decided he could not use one word for both the shouting constable and Shreya, so he judged each person on what they did instead of painting all police alike.

qa.q: What might the girl have felt when Shreya put the raincoat on her?
qa.a: The girl was probably frightened and cold while alone, and Shreya's kind questions and coat may have made her feel safer until her mother came.

grounding: A citizen sees an officer patiently help a lost child and updates a harsh view, judging fairly instead of painting everyone alike.

passage:
Jaya was on her way to work when a scooter skidded on the wet road and an elderly rider fell hard beside the divider. Traffic swelled and people stood filming. Constable Indu got there first. She stopped the cars with one hand, knelt beside the man, and said, "Stay still, uncle. Help is coming."
She called the ambulance, held his hand, and asked a bystander to bring water. When the ambulance arrived she wrote down the details and the rider's son's number.
Jaya remembered the year a police desk had brushed away her own complaint, and how sour that had made her. She watched Indu quietly and thought, some are like this too. She put her phone away and offered to help clear the road.

qa.q: What did Indu say to the elderly rider?
qa.a: Indu said, 'Stay still, uncle. Help is coming.'

qa.q: What was Jaya feeling as she watched Indu?
qa.a: Jaya felt her sourness soften and some respect, as she remembered how a police desk had brushed off her complaint.

qa.q: What choice did Jaya make after watching Indu, and what did it show?
qa.a: Jaya put her phone away and offered to help clear the road, and her thought that some are like this too shows she was judging individuals fairly.

qa.q: How might the elderly rider have felt while Indu knelt beside him?
qa.a: He was probably frightened and in pain after the fall, and Indu's calm voice and held hand likely made him feel safer until the ambulance came.

grounding: A citizen sees an officer patiently help an accident victim and updates a harsh view, judging fairly instead of painting everyone alike.
